title: Supply curves and utilization matrix by instance family
summary: Working worksheet that models supply-side cost curves and a utilization matrix broken out by GPU instance family and region. Goal: give product and finance an actionable view of marginal $/GPU-hour across procurement slabs, expected throughput per GPU for our common request shapes, and a reconciled $/1M tokens estimate for planning conversations.
assumptions: Primary request profile: 4-token prompt + 256-token completion average (seq len 260) for latencysensitive endpoints
Concurrency per GPU baseline: measured 6 concurrent sessions for A100-80GB equivalent under optimized kernel stack
Burst capacity is priced 25% above reserved slab rate (cloud burst on-demand premium)
Network & infra overhead (orchestration, storage, misc) amortized as $0.45/GPU-hour
Quantization/throughput improvements assumed for one alternative slab: -25% GPU-hour per token when using 8-bit optimized kernels
supply_curve_notes: We treat supply as piecewise steps (reserved, reserved+spot mix, on-demand) per region and instance family. Each step has a volume cap and an effective marginal price. For planning we collapse spot variability into three bands: low availability (-20% capacity, -30% price), nominal, and constrained (+40% price). Slab sizing should target the inflection points of cost-per-throughput where marginal cost increases steeply. Important: capacity elasticity differs by instance family because smaller GPUs let us pack more parallel sessions but have higher per-token overhead.

sensitivity_scenarios: High-demand winter campaign: +2x request volume for 6 weeks; examine slab refill thresholds and 95th-percentile marginal price
Spot-churn shock: spot capacity drops 50% regionally for 72 hours; simulate effects on $/1M tokens when forced onto on-demand slab
Quantization rollout: 8-bit kernels enabled on 30% of models reducing GPU-hours-per-token by 25%; compute net blended price
New-region expansion: add ap-northeast with introductory on-demand at +15% price but no reserved capacity for first quarter
actions: Prioritize reserved commitments for A100-80GB in us-west1 to cover 60% of baseline steady-state demand
Create an operational playbook to move non-latency-critical workloads (embeddings/batch reranking) to T4 slab during spot-rich windows
Run a week-long benchmark for H100-80GB on retrieval-heavy prompts to verify tokens_per_gpu_hour (current estimate is conservative)
Add a finance dashboard tile that surfaces marginal $/1M tokens by route and by region for the last 7 days
finance_followup: Ask finance to provide current committed discount schedule by provider and region (explicit discount tiers for 12/24 month reserved buys). Request a mapping of actual invoice lineitems for the last 3 months to reconcile our amortized overhead assumption. Also flag: exchange-rate exposure for eu/apac price buckets needs explicit hedge recommendation from treasury.
in-line_calcs_reference: blended_gpu_price = (reserved_volume * reserved_price + on_demand_volume * on_demand_price + spot_volume * spot_price) / total_volume
